title: Asirgarh Fort
scope: The surviving hilltop Asirgarh Fort above Burhanpur, with the upper stone rampart, interpreted west terraces of Kamargarh and Malaygarh, gate masonry, twin-minaret mosque and mapped reservoirs.
limitations: Current survey geometry anchors the upper line and three reservoirs. Lower west sections, tower sizes and any wall fragments away from the native footprint are approximate reconciliations of the 1880 plan with open elevation data.
The original open elevation cannot resolve the abrupt basalt lip at every point. The model fits foundations to the source surface. Wall losses and unmeasured heights are interpreted.

The summit ensemble includes the mosque exterior as a bounded reconstruction. Religious interiors, the rock-cut temple rooms, unidentified roofless structures, lost barracks and water depths are outside its scope.
